title: Craig interpolation: the vocabulary shared by a consequence
summary: Factor a first-order consequence through a statement using only the symbols present on both sides.
abstract: A sentence may imply another sentence even though each mentions functions or relations absent from the other. Craig's interpolation theorem says that their shared vocabulary is enough to express a statement lying between them: the first sentence implies it, and it implies the second. We prove this using the preceding construction that joins compatible theories. We then replace a finite tuple of free variables by fresh constants to obtain the corresponding result for formulas. Examples show how a private function disappears behind an existence statement, and why a language with no nonlogical symbols can still express a restriction on the size of a domain.
